title: Why does metal feel colder than wood?

shots.intent: Frame the Observer beside both samples only long enough to establish the sensory puzzle; the character is present because they will test the materials.
Remove the Observer from frame and let the two samples own the shot while their equal condition is established.

effects.purpose: Connects the samples as one temperature condition.

shots.intent: Bring the Observer back specifically to touch the metal; the fast stream and immediate flinch make the sensation causal rather than decorative.

effects.purpose: Fast conduction from skin into metal.

shots.intent: Repeat the experiment with the opposite hand on wood, but keep the performance calm while the stream is visibly sparse and slow.
Remove the character again and resolve on the two materials themselves so the final takeaway is the comparison, not the mascot.

effects.purpose: Re-centers the comparison as the conceptual answer.
